references.text: Rachel names her first son Joseph and asks for another son—a prayer fulfilled with Benjamin's birth, but which costs her life.
Context before Benjamin's birth: Rachel has severe labor pains during childbirth.
Rachel dies and is buried on the way to Ephrath (Bethlehem), and Jacob sets up a memorial pillar over her grave.
Judah describes Benjamin as the surviving son of Jacob's beloved wife, referencing his brother Joseph's death and their mother's passing.
Jacob recalls Rachel's death during the journey to Ephrath when he blesses Joseph's sons.
Phinehas' wife names her son Ichabod as she dies in childbirth—a thematic parallel to Rachel naming Ben-Oni on her deathbed.
A strong theological contrast between naming in response to prayer (life) and naming at death (grief).
A deep theological parallel about God's ability to give new life and hope after great loss (Seth instead of Abel; Benjamin instead of Ben-Oni).
A parallel about naming that transforms grief/loss into hope and restoration (Naomi's emptiness filled by Obed; Rachel's death turned into Benjamin's life).
